The Trench Funnel thesis synthesizes 75 cross-domain facts into a unified causal framework. It begins with atmospheric conditions (air density and wind) that alter ball physics, followed by injury-driven roster shifts affecting positional load, and concludes with in-season tracking data refining player efficiency. Each primitive operates within distinct but interlinked regimes—environmental aerodynamics, injury propagation, and real-time performance metrics. The failure mode occurs when any component lacks empirical grounding, such as assuming static efficiency without tracking input or ignoring wind effects on carry distance. Dualities emerge between static injury reports and dynamic tracking, where the former sets initial expectations and the latter adjusts them. The system's robustness depends on continuous validation of each causal link through telemetry.
